title: Settings
description: Request handling, access and maintenance for this proxy. Each card saves on its own.
discardBody: Some settings cards have changes that are not saved. Leaving this page discards them.
allowOverUsageHint: Accounts keep serving requests after their credits run out.
usageRefresh.title: Background usage refresh
usageRefresh.hint: How often the proxy checks every account's credits and renews tokens about to expire. When off, usage updates only when you refresh an account.
lenientStreamIntegrityHint: Kiro marks a turn complete with a stop reason or a metering event. Some IdC and Enterprise accounts send neither, so their replies are rejected as truncated.
lenientStreamIntegrityRisk: Only for affected accounts: a cut-off reply can pass as complete.
routingMode.title: Routing mode
routingMode.weightedHint: New requests rotate across the enabled accounts. An account with weight N takes about N times as many.
routingMode.priorityHint: New requests go to the account with the lowest priority number. When it is cooling down, out of credits, disabled or lacks the model, the next one takes over.
routingMode.priorityMore: Set each account's priority in its detail sheet. Accounts with the same number keep their list order. While conversations are kept on one account, a running conversation stays on the account that answered its last turn, even after a higher-priority account becomes available again; turn that off for strict priority on every request.
rpmLimitHint: An account that started this many requests in the last minute is skipped until the minute passes. When every account is at the limit, new requests get a 429 error.
rpmLimitMore: Off by default. Retries on the same account do not count again; a move to another account counts there. The Accounts page shows each account's requests per minute and today.
rpmLimitInvalid: Requests per minute must be a whole number between 1 and {max}.
sessionAffinityHint: Follow-up turns go back to the account that answered the previous turn, which already holds the prompt cache. Turn this off to route every request fresh by the routing mode.
sessionAffinityMore: New conversations are still routed by the routing mode. If that account is cooling down, out of credits or failing, the request moves to another account.
selfHeal.enable: Bring back accounts the proxy blocked
selfHeal.hint: When no account can serve, the proxy lifts the auth bans and error cooldowns it set by itself and tries again.
selfHeal.more: Kiro suspensions, accounts you turned off and quota cooldowns are never touched: a quota cooldown runs until the usage resets. A healed account that fails again is blocked again.
selfHeal.intervalInvalid: Enter a whole number of seconds from {min} to {max}.
selfHeal.rounds: Heals in a row without a successful request
selfHeal.roundsHint: From 0 to {max}; 0 means no limit. Past it, the proxy stops healing until a request succeeds or you resume.
selfHeal.roundsInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {max}.
selfHeal.never: The proxy has not needed to heal any account yet.
selfHeal.roundsUsed: {used} of {max} heals used since the last successful request.
selfHeal.roundsUsedUnlimited_one: {count} heal since the last successful request (no limit).
selfHeal.roundsUsedUnlimited_other: {count} heals since the last successful request (no limit).
selfHeal.halted: Self-heal stopped: the limit was reached with no successful request. Check the accounts, then resume.
selfHeal.toastHealed_one: Self-heal brought {count} account back into rotation.
selfHeal.toastHealed_other: Self-heal brought {count} accounts back into rotation.
selfHeal.toastHalted: Self-heal stopped: accounts keep failing after a heal. Check them.
autoContinueEnable: Continue answers cut off by the output limit
autoContinueHint: Kiro stops a single answer at about 8192 output tokens. When an answer stops there without a tool call, the proxy asks Kiro to continue and appends the rest.
autoContinueMore: Usage is summed across requests. Each continuation is another billed upstream request, and the seams can occasionally repeat or skip a few words.
autoContinueMaxHint: Between 1 and 10. Continuation also stops at the client's own {param}.
autoContinueMaxInvalid: Maximum continuations must be a whole number between 1 and {max}.
structuredToolHistory: Send earlier tool calls as structured tool calls
structuredToolHistoryHint: Earlier tool calls and results reach the model as real tool calls, so long agent sessions keep calling tools. Turn this off to always send earlier tool activity as plain text.
structuredToolHistoryMore: A pair falls back to plain text when the request does not declare that tool or the call and result IDs do not match. If Kiro rejects the structured form, the proxy retries once with plain text and keeps using plain text for an hour.
imageResizeEnable: Shrink large images before sending them
imageResizeHint: Kiro rejects very large images, such as full-screen screenshots. An image over either limit below is scaled down, keeping its aspect ratio, and re-encoded before it goes upstream. Smaller images are sent unchanged.
imageResizeMore: Images are re-encoded as JPEG at quality 85. A transparent PNG stays PNG when the result fits the size limit; otherwise it is placed on white. An animated GIF keeps only its first frame. An image the proxy cannot decode is sent unchanged.
imageResizeMaxDimensionHint: In pixels, between 256 and 4096. Claude itself scales larger images down to about 1568.
imageResizeMaxDimensionInvalid: Maximum width or height must be a whole number between {min} and {max}.
imageResizeMaxKBHint: In KB, between 50 and 4096. A larger image is compressed further, then made smaller if it still does not fit.
imageResizeMaxKBInvalid: Maximum file size must be a whole number between {min} and {max}.
thinkingHint: Choose the model suffix that turns on thinking and how thinking output reaches each API.
thinkingSuffixHint: Add this suffix to a model name to turn on thinking, for example {example}.
modelMappingsHint: Map client model names to Kiro model IDs. Rules run in order, and the first rule whose text appears in the model name wins. A model Kiro serves itself only follows a rule with its full name.
modelMappings.resetBody_one: Your {count} mapping is replaced by the {defaults} defaults when you save.
modelMappings.resetBody_other: Your {count} mappings are replaced by the {defaults} defaults when you save.
modelMappings.editorDescription: Requests whose model name contains the text go to the Kiro model instead.
modelMappings.matchHint: Matches when this text appears anywhere in the client's model name, in any case. A model Kiro serves itself is only redirected by a rule with its full name. Rules run top to bottom; the first match wins.
modelMappings.targetHint: The Kiro model ID the request uses instead.
modelMappings.resetNote: An empty list is not kept after a restart. The proxy then uses the defaults.
modelMappings.noRules: No model mappings. Direct Claude model IDs still work.
modelMappings.dragInstructions: To pick up a mapping, press Space or Enter. Use the arrow keys to move it, Space or Enter to drop it, and Escape to cancel.
modelMappings.dragCancel: Reordering canceled. Mapping {from} stays in place.
endpointSettingsHint: Choose which Kiro endpoint receives requests.
endpointHint: Automatic picks an endpoint based on availability.
endpointFallbackHint: When off, only the selected endpoint is used.
upstream.title: Upstream domain & region
upstream.hint: Where the proxy sends requests to Kiro. These settings apply to every account from the next request on.
upstream.domainHint: Kiro (kiro.dev) is the host newer Kiro clients use for chat and web search. Usage and model lists stay on AWS.
upstream.effectiveHost: The Kiro IDE endpoint and web search go to {host}.
upstream.effectiveHostAuto: The Kiro IDE endpoint and web search go to {host}, in each account's own region.
upstream.apiRegionHint: Overrides the region of every account's requests. Kiro rejects requests when the region does not match the account's profile.
upstream.authRegionHint: The region every Builder ID and IAM Identity Center token is refreshed in. Leave it empty unless an account's region is wrong.
upstream.authRegionInvalid: Enter an AWS region code, such as us-east-1.
adminPasswordHint: Changing the password ends every other signed-in session. This browser stays signed in.
passwordTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
proxyHint: Send Kiro and sign-in traffic through a SOCKS5, HTTP or HTTPS proxy. Changes apply right away, without a restart.
proxyNoneHint: Connect from this server's own network and IP address.
proxySocks5Hint: Tunnel each connection. Works with SSH tunnels and most VPN apps.
proxyHttpHint: Use HTTP CONNECT, over HTTP or HTTPS. Common on company and cloud networks.
proxyProtocolHint: HTTPS also encrypts the link to the proxy, its password included. The proxy must accept TLS.
proxyPasteTip: Paste a full URL such as {example} to fill every field.
proxyRemoveBody: Kiro and sign-in traffic will leave from this server's own IP address right away.
proxyApplyNote: Saving switches Kiro and sign-in traffic to this proxy right away.
responseHeadersHint: Add your own headers to every API response, streamed or not, errors included. Values can hold variables, for example to match NewAPI or OneAPI logs to this proxy's request log.
responseHeaders.timing: Headers are filled in when a response starts, with what is known at that moment. A stream starts with its first event, so {account} is the account that streams the answer. A header whose value comes out empty is left out, and a header the proxy sets itself, such as Cache-Control on a stream, is kept.
responseHeaders.empty: No custom headers yet. For example, {example} lets NewAPI or OneAPI match their logs to this proxy's request log.
responseHeaders.limit: You can add up to {max} headers.
responseHeaders.editorDescription: Sent on every response of /v1/messages, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/models and count_tokens.
responseHeaders.name: Header name
responseHeaders.nameHint: Letters, digits and symbols such as - or _, with no spaces. Headers the proxy manages, such as Content-Type, Connection or CORS headers, are refused.
responseHeaders.valueHint: Text and variables, on one line, up to {max} bytes.
responseHeaders.var.request_id: A new ID for each request. The request log shows it as Trace ID.
responseHeaders.var.model: The model the client asked for. Empty on /v1/models and when the request body cannot be read.
responseHeaders.var.account_id: The ID of the Kiro account that answers. Empty when no account was called, such as for count_tokens.
responseHeaders.var.key_id: The ID of the client's API key. Empty when API keys are not required.
responseHeaders.var.client_ip: The client's IP address as this server sees it. X-Forwarded-For is not read.
responseHeaders.error.nameInvalid: A header name uses letters, digits and symbols such as - _ . ~, with no spaces or colons.
responseHeaders.error.nameTooLong: A header name can be at most {max} characters.
responseHeaders.error.nameForbidden: The proxy manages {name}, so it cannot be set here.
responseHeaders.error.valueInvalid: The value cannot contain line breaks or control characters.
responseHeaders.error.valueTooLong: The value can be at most {max} bytes.
promptFilterHint: Clean system prompts before they reach Kiro. Built-in filters run first, then custom rules in list order.
filterClaudeCode: Replace Claude Code CLI system prompts
filterClaudeCodeHint: Detects Claude Code's built-in system prompt and swaps it for a compact backend prompt. The other filters and rules then skip it.
filterEnvNoiseHint: Removes injected environment variables, git status, recent commits and similar noise from system prompts.
customRulesHint: A line filter drops every line that contains its text, in any case. A regex rule replaces each match; {group} inserts a captured group.
promptFilter.name: Rule name
promptFilter.invalidRegex: This regex does not compile; the proxy skips it.
promptFilter.matchHintContains: Every line that contains this text is removed. Case is ignored.
promptFilter.matchHintRegex: A Go (RE2) regular expression. Every match is replaced.
promptFilter.replaceHint: Leave empty to delete the match. {group} inserts a captured group.
logRetentionHint: Request and error log entries are deleted after the number of days below, so the database stops growing. Overview totals and the model mix still count them.
logRetentionMore: Cleanup runs two minutes after the server starts, then once a day, and right after you save. It deletes in small batches, so requests are not held up. New entries reuse the freed space; the database file itself does not shrink.
logRetentionDaysHint: Between 1 and {max}. The Requests page shows only the entries kept.
logRetentionDaysInvalid: Days must be a whole number between 1 and {max}.
logRetentionNeverRun: No cleanup since the server started
logRetentionArchived_one: {n} removed request still counted in totals
logRetentionArchived_other: {n} removed requests still counted in totals
resetStatsHint: Deletes request history and error logs. Per-account and per-key usage stay.
confirmResetBody: Request history and error logs are deleted. Per-account and per-key usage stay. This cannot be undone.
